title: fix(objectql): an in-process engine verb refuses an object name the registry does not resolve (#21516)
body:
Part of #21516

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

This narrows the in-process engine verbs' accept set: a target name the schema
registry does not resolve is now refused with the data door's own
`OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` (404), instead of being handed to the driver as a raw table
name. One name space for the in-process verbs and the door (triage ruling).
No surface is widened.

**This PR does not close #21516 by itself — `Part of`, not `Fixes`.** The
engine change is complete and correct; what remains is a decision on how far to
carry the implied test migration (see "Open decision" below). The security
posture clause ("don't widen the PR") and the ruling's own stop clause both
point the scope question back to the seat.

## What changed

- **`packages/core` (new `objectNotFoundError`).** One factory for the
  `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` / 404 envelope, beside `recordNotFoundError` and for the
  same ADR-0076 D2 reason (the engine closure cannot import the package where
  the door's envelope was written). Both doors now build the refusal here.
- **`packages/metadata-protocol` (the door).** `assertObjectRegistered` raises
  that shared factory — same wire, same code, no new message.
- **`packages/objectql` (the engine).** `resolveObjectName` throws
  `objectNotFoundError` for a name the registry does not resolve, rather than
  returning it as a physical table name. Every in-process verb
  (`find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`,
  `validate`) resolves through it, so all refuse uniformly — no spelling
  allow-list, no per-caller marker. `judgeFilter` keeps judging the filter for
  an unresolved name (it reads nothing and reaches no driver), as its contract
  states.
- **Three platform-internal, constant-name best-effort probes** that read a
  known system object and are already fail-soft on a missing table now treat
  the engine's refusal (attributed to their own object) as the same
  "not provisioned in this composition" case — a path a body cannot reach,
  never the resolver's old raw-table fall-through:
  `ObjectQL.probeInstallOrganizations`,
  `SeedLoaderService.resolveSoleOrganizationId`, and
  `SysMetadataRepository`'s history counters.

## Why (disclosure discipline: classes, doors, roles, codes only)

An action body invoked through the actions door could name a protected member
of the stored-metadata family by a spelling the registry does not resolve and
receive its stored content, whether a member or an administrator invoked it,
because the in-process verb handed that name to the driver as a raw table name
and every name-keyed in-process guard — including PR #21513's reader seam — was
addressed by the registered name only. The generic data door answers
`OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` for the same name. The engine now answers the same, so the
two doors share one name space and the guard cannot be stepped around.

Measured (engine level, control + refusal): a registered name serves (control);
an unregistered spelling that resolves to a protected family table is refused
`OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` / 404. Before this change the same read served the row — the
`#3770` pin (`protocol-unregistered-object.test.ts`, case B) asserts exactly
that serve on `origin/main` and goes red against this change; PR #21513's
finding 3 measured the same exit at the public actions door.

## Census — does any legitimate platform reader rely on the raw-table fall-through?

Instrumented the resolver's fall-through and ran the `objectql`,
`metadata-protocol` and `runtime` suites, plus a full boot + seed + door drive
of four example apps (crm, showcase, todo, multi-package).

| composition | fall-through reads | reader relies on it? |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 4 example apps booted, seeded, driven through the doors | **0** | no — every platform reader addresses a registered object |
| unit/integration suites (partial registries + tolerant stub drivers) | many | only test harnesses, plus the three constant-name probes below |

Every in-repo caller that passes a possibly-unresolved name, by function:

| caller | object (constant) | pre-change | disposition |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `ObjectQL.probeInstallOrganizations` | the org object | fail-soft on missing table | moved: registry-presence → empty |
| `SeedLoaderService.resolveSoleOrganizationId` | the org object | fail-soft on missing table | moved: recognise the refusal as not-provisioned |
| `SysMetadataRepository` history counters | the history object | fail-soft on missing table | moved: recognise the refusal as not-provisioned |
| `ObjectQL.cascadeDeleteRelations` / `planCascadeAtomicity` / `referenceExists` | a relation ref | already `try/catch` | unchanged — already tolerate a throw |
| the data door's existence gate | the requested name | raised the 404 itself | now raises the shared factory |

Conclusion: **no production or example reader relies on the fall-through.** The
three constant-name probes read a known system object and were already fail-soft
for its absence; they now recognise the engine's refusal as that same absence.

## Named gaps (open decision)

The uniform engine refusal changes the behaviour of the org probe for an
**unregistered** org object from "reach the driver, fail soft, withhold the
noise" to "refused by the engine before the driver." That ripples into test
pins that encode the old fall-through:

- `packages/objectql`: unit tests that drive an **unregistered** object on
  purpose (type-blind lowering, the `#3770` gate, aggregate/temporal/filter
  doors, undeclared-field paths) must now assert the refusal; metadata-write
  harnesses that register only part of the stored-metadata family must register
  the family the repository requires.
- `packages/runtime`: the fail-soft org-probe **noise discipline** (`#12852` /
  `#7929`) is asserted across ~12 files that expect the probe to reach the
  driver for an unregistered org object; those pins need reshaping.
- This narrows recorded decision `#3770` ("the engine deliberately does not
  reject; internal callers unaffected") and ADR-0053's type-blind lowering
  (preserved for a registered field-less object; removed for an unregistered
  name — the bypass). Reshaping those recorded disciplines is the scope the
  seat should confirm.

PR #21513's reader-seam pins stay green (23/23 with this change).
